## Integrating Convex Finance using OptyFi's DeFi Adapter Interface

### Prize Bounty
5000 USDC

### Description
The bounty is to build an integration with Convex Finance’s liquidity pools using OptyFi's DeFi Adapter interface and [defi-legos](https://github.com/Opty-Fi/defi-legos) library. With this integration, OptyFi users should be able to deposit CRV, CVX and Curve LP tokens into OptyFi vaults which will in turn deploy them into Convex to earn yield boosted by CRV and CVX rewards. The OptyFi Protocol should also be able to deposit CRV and Curve LP tokens acquired from other strategies involving our direct Curve integration.

The overall goal is to maximize the liquidity, utility and profitability of CRV and other Curve assets in DeFi.

### Resources
https://github.com/Opty-Fi/defi-legos - This should help in implementing adapter contracts and data for unit tests 
https://opty.fi/ - This should help to give you a good high-level understanding of OptyFi and what we’re building. https://docs.opty.fi/ - Here you can find more information on the OptyFi Protocol including tokens, pools, vaults, strategies, risk framework, DeFi Adapters and optimization engine. https://github.com/Opty-Fi/defi-adapter-kit - Please refer to Readme.md, contracts/ and test/ for in-depth technical knowledge. https://www.convexfinance.com/

title: [Bounty] Create a sett style auto-compounding LP token vault
body:
We want to move from geysers to Sett style vaults for our rewards, based on yearn vaults. 

We want this sett vault to be useable for LP providers for SGT ETH. 
It should have an accompanying strategy that allows it to auto-compound earnings in SGT by providing them as liquidity to uniswap, and selling any required to create the ETH side. 

Should have documentation for functionality and deployment. 
Should be tested on a testnet. We can send you SGT to test with on goerli.  

Bonus high value requirement: 
- Allow users to choose a lockup period for their principal. 
- Allow reward rate modification based on the lockup period. 
- Allow locked user funds to be used for voting either via a voter proxy contract or functionality in the contract. Or in the worst case a vote-escrow derivative ERC20 as used by CRV. 
This time-locked vote-escrow mechanism is up for debate in terms of implementation details and how it should ideally function. We are open to ideas. .

title: [Minter] Add solo staking
body:
Users should be able to use our contract for solo staking. 
To start we would require users to have the following: 
- 32 ETH
- 1000 SGT bonded and timelocked in a way that admins can unlock it when the users exit their validators or slash it if the user acts in a nefarious way.   

For this we will need to upgrade the send2eth2 function in the minter to use AccessControl over having a single owner.  

For a simplified implementation, the SGT bonded user should be able to call the function directly, resulting in a deposit function call which returns 32 vETH2 to them in exchange for 32.1 ETH.  

The solo staker can then use their vETH2 to earn profits at a higher APY in our ecosystem while waiting for ETH2 rewards to be unlocked via a chain merge or other mechanism the EF comes up with.  

This way the solo staker holds onto both their private keys for withdrawals and the validator. 

The solo staker will be responsible for running their own validator to start with and entering the correct public keys for the call registering the validator.

title: IssueDetailPage's escrow status label says "Funds locked" for paid, refunded, and expired bounties, even though funds have already left escrow in all three cases

labels.name: very hard
labels.description: Very difficult task, expert-level effort required

labels.name: Stellar Wave
labels.description: Issues in the Stellar wave program

body:
`src/app/issues/[id]/page.tsx#IssueDetailPage` renders the escrow status card as: ```tsx

{bounty.status === "open" ? "Awaiting funding" : "Funds locked"}

``` This binary ternary only distinguishes `"open"` (not yet funded) from every other status, labeling all of them "Funds locked" — including `"paid"` (funds already released to the contributor), `"refunded"` (funds already returned to the sponsor), and `"expired"` (deadline passed). For all three of these terminal states, funds are specifically **not** locked in escrow anymore — that's what makes them terminal — yet the UI's dedicated "Escrow status" card tells the viewer the opposite. A sponsor checking on a bounty they refunded weeks ago, or a contributor checking a bounty they were already paid for, sees "Funds locked" under "Escrow status" — directly contradicting the actual on-chain state this card exists to summarize, on the one page in the app whose whole purpose is showing accurate escrow status for a specific bounty. Suggested fix: expand this to a proper mapping covering all `BountyStatus` values — e.g. "Awaiting funding" (open), "Funds locked" (funded/claimed/in_review/merged), "Paid out" (paid), "Refunded to sponsor" (refunded), "Expired, unclaimed" (expired) — instead of the current two-way open/everything-else split.

title: Bounty winner selection integrity: user with highest impressions/engagement did not receive the $1000 prize
body:
## Summary

A user who won the \$1000 bounty for most impressions/comments/engagement was not awarded the prize — a different user with lower numbers received it instead. This indicates either a scoring calculation bug, a leaderboard display bug, or a manual override with no transparent criteria.

## Problem

The bounty was awarded for the highest impressions/comments/engagement metric. The user with the winning numbers did not receive the payout; a participant with objectively lower numbers did. No explanation or audit trail was provided to the community.

Discord: https://discord.com/channels/1470856511193616498/1521660798492213249

## Possible causes

- **Scoring bug:** The leaderboard or winner-selection logic is computing engagement metrics incorrectly (e.g. not summing across all posts, using stale cached counts, applying wrong time window)
- **Display bug:** The leaderboard shows different numbers than what the backend uses to determine the winner — user sees they're winning but backend picks differently
- **Eligibility filter applied silently:** A hidden eligibility criterion (account age, verified status, etc.) disqualified the apparent winner without surfacing this to them
- **Manual override without disclosure:** Winner was selected manually without announcing the criteria change

## Fix scope

- [ ] Audit the bounty winner-selection query: confirm it pulls the correct metric (impressions + comments + engagement), correct time window, and correct participant set
- [ ] Add a public leaderboard that shows the live ranking and the exact metric being measured — no surprises at payout time
- [ ] If eligibility filters exist (account age, verification, etc.), surface them clearly on the bounty detail page before the bounty closes
- [ ] Add an audit log for bounty winner selection: which query ran, what scores were returned, which entry was selected and why
- [ ] Notify the apparent runner-up if they were disqualified by an eligibility filter, with the specific reason

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Bounty winner selection is deterministic and auditable — same input data always produces the same winner
- [ ] Leaderboard displayed to users uses the identical metric and query that determines the winner
- [ ] Eligibility criteria are shown on the bounty page before entry
- [ ] Admin bounty payout panel shows winner selection rationale (query result + score)
- [ ] Post-resolution: review the specific bounty in question and confirm whether the correct winner was paid

## Related

- #134 — Bounty creation fails with HTTP 400
- #180 — Bounty stuck in review
- #243, #262 — Bounty approval failures
- Bounty payout flow (escrow → winner)

title: bounty: board daemon idle-dies mid-session (idle-died 4x, even with a keep-alive tail)
body:
## What bit

The bounty board daemon **idle-dies during an active session**. In one dream-flute team session (via anthill) it died **4 times** — even with a host keep-alive `tail` running — and was ultimately abandoned as unreliable. The team fell back to the grapevine + git history as the durable record.

Because the board can vanish mid-session, any ritual that treats "settle the board" as a required step deadlocks or gets abandoned.

## Ask

- The daemon should **survive idle** for the length of a working session (heartbeat/keep-alive that actually holds), or
- fail **loudly and recoverably** (clear "board is down, restart with X") rather than silently going unresponsive.

## Context / provenance

Surfaced upstream from the **anthill** team-OS plugin during a dream-flute dogfood session. anthill is separately softening its finalize-session ritual to treat the board as best-effort (git+vine are the durable record) — but the underlying idle-death is a bounty-daemon reliability bug. Env: darwin 25.5.0 · Bun 1.3.14 · spellbook (bounty).

title: bounty: surface wordmark still renders "Tuskboard" — regenerate as Bounty
body:
## What
The bounty surface's wordmark image (`plugins/spellbook/skills/bounty/assets/wordmark.webp`) visibly renders **"Tuskboard"** — the spell's former name.

## Why it slipped
The `bounty-agent-usable` migration's branding check was `grep -rni tuskboard`, which returns clean because **grep can't see into a binary `.webp`**. The text was all migrated; the wordmark *image* still carries the old brand. Caught during the Alpine surface port's browser verification.

## Impact
This is a **live Tuskboard mark in the surface**, which violates the `bounty-agent-usable` success criterion *"No live Tuskboard string remains in the bounty spell surface/contract."* That criterion was explicitly **deferred** for the migration branch (per maintainer) and split out here as a follow-up.

## Fix
Regenerate a **Bounty** wordmark asset (image generation — imago / media-forge, not a find-replace) matching the surface palette, and replace `assets/wordmark.webp`.

## Context
Follow-up from the bounty house-pattern migration (`docs/projects/bounty-agent-usable/`); tracked as merge-gate item **W1** in that project's `backlog.md`.
